transcript:
Meeting header:
2027-10-01 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Gupta (Redwood CSM); Dr. Emily Zhang, Marcus Lee, Rosa Martinez, Jamal Ortiz (Mariner Medical)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff, clarify success criteria and security needs, agree pilot approach and owners.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer and Samir who's our CSM. Quick roll call?
00:12 Emily: Hi hi, Emily here, CTO at Mariner.
00:15 Marcus: Marcus Lee, I run engineering.
00:18 Rosa: Rosa Martinez, security.
00:20 Jamal: Jamal Ortiz, product.
00:25 Alex: Awesome. We'll keep this to about 45-60 min, go over the onboarding plan, security, pilot and who's doing what. Priya, do you want to take the technical primer?
00:34 Priya: Sure — thanks Alex. Just a quick note on Redwood's deployment options, we have hosted API, dedicated/reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem options. For onboarding we usually recommend starting on hosted to validate the prompts and success criteria, then move to dedicated if you need predictable throughput. And for regulated data you can do Private with a customer-managed VPC and KMS integration.
01:05 Marcus: Quick question — when you say dedicated, is that like a single-tenant GPU cluster or shared but reserved?
01:12 Priya: It's reserved capacity — GPU pools that are dedicated to your account. It's single-tenant in the sense of capacity allocation and isolation, but the control plane is still Redwood unless you go full private. There's some nuance in how KV cache and batching behave across pools, but we can dig in on the deep dive.
01:33 Rosa: On encryption — we need to know about KMS/HSM integrations and where keys live. Also SOC 2 and audit logs, retention, that sort of thing.
01:42 Samir: Absolutely. We'll send the SOC 2 summary and our security pack. For keys we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and we can discuss bring-your-own-key in the enterprise plan.
01:55 Emily: For the pilot we don't plan to send PHI, but some data could be sensitive. We want SSO in place and RBAC before we move past pilot.
02:05 Alex: Makes sense. Action: we'll share the SSO/SAML guide and a checklist for RBAC.

02:20 Jamal: Thinking about success criteria — our main KPI is extraction accuracy from clinical notes for coding suggestions. Secondary is latency under 300ms for the UI flows. Cost is a factor but accuracy first.
02:35 Priya: Good — for extraction accuracy we'll want a prompt set and sample evals. We can run a few evals on hosted, show tradeoffs and suggest quantized variants for cost. Latency under 300ms is doable for short prompts on Dedicated — on hosted it depends on model choice and batch behavior.
03:00 Marcus: Do you have a recommended model family? We're leaning open models to avoid per-query surprises.
03:07 Priya: We typically recommend Redwood-verified open models for production, and we can provide performance profiles. For latency-sensitive UI flows we might use a smaller LM or a generation-limited pipeline. We can also use caching/prefix caching for repeated patient templates.
03:30 Rosa: Any log retention policies for debug vs PII? We need to ensure no raw text is retained beyond what we agree.
03:38 Samir: We'll add a retention configuration to the onboarding checklist. By default hosted retains logs for x days for debugging, but for enterprise we can configure stricter policies and data purge with audit logs. We'll send the doc.

04:00 Alex: Ok let's walk through the proposed timeline — quick pilot running for 4 weeks, two sprint cycles. Week 1: integrations (SSO + API keys), Week 2: run evals and tune prompts, Week 3: performance testing and canary, Week 4: review and go/no-go. Does that align?
04:20 Marcus: That's tight but doable. We need SE support for performance tests in Week 3.
04:25 Priya: I'll own performance tests with Marcus' team. We'll need a small dedicated trial if you want consistent latency numbers, but we can also do synthetic benchmarking on hosted first.
04:38 Marcus: Synthetic is fine to start. If synthetic looks good we'll request a short reserved capacity trial.
04:44 Jamal: Who will own the prompt evaluation and the ground-truth labeling? We'll need to loop in our clinical SME.
04:50 Emily: I'll assign the SME. Jamal will coordinate.

05:05 Rosa: On compliance review — timeline wise we need the SOC2 and penetration test summary before we approve any production rollout. Can you provide contact for security vetting?
05:14 Samir: Yes, that's me. I'll be the point for security. I'll also schedule a follow-up call with your security team.
05:21 Rosa: Great. Also please include a data flow diagram for Hosted vs Private deployment; we need specifics on egress, logs, and key handling.
05:30 Priya: Noted — we'll provide data flow diagrams and architecture sketches. We'll attach links in the follow-up email.

06:00 Alex: Any competitors or prior vendors you're comparing us against?
06:05 Jamal: We're looking at Anthropic and OpenAI for the hosted piece, and evaluating Bedrock for the integrated cloud option. Cost and enterprise controls are the differentiators.
06:15 Alex: Understood, we'll include a short competitive note and show where Redwood's Dedicated and Private options give you controls for keys and auditability.

06:30 Priya: Quick nitty-gritty: for the pilot we typically set up a single API route for the extraction model, enable streaming off for batch tests, and configure a small prefix cache for repeated patient templates. Also will want to collect a 200-sample prompt set for evals.
06:55 Marcus: We'll prepare samples. How do you handle model rollouts / canarying if we move to production?
07:05 Priya: We support per-route rollouts: canary traffic split, automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model, and tracing hooks so you can correlate requests to application logs.
07:20 Emily: Nice. For auditing we want to ensure request IDs map back to users — SSO linking would help.
07:27 Samir: We'll include mapping guidelines in the RBAC/SSO doc.

07:45 Alex: Any blockers we haven't covered?
07:48 Rosa: We need to see the strict data retention and KMS details. Also whether we can have a dedicated compliance session.
07:55 Samir: We'll schedule that.
08:00 Jamal: Pricing — curious about committed reserved pricing for Dedicated. Can you send options?
08:06 Alex: Yes, I'll send reserved capacity tiers and monthly/annual commit options. For pilot we can start on hosted to avoid commit.
08:12 Marcus: That works. If pilot shows good results we'll likely request Dedicated trial for Week 3.

08:25 Priya: I'll also put together a perf test plan: endpoints, synthetic load, target latency distributions, and metrics to capture (p50/p95/p99, token throughput).
08:40 Jamal: For integration, who sets up API keys and how do we rotate them?
08:44 Samir: CSM or AE will create initial keys and we recommend using short-lived key rotation and vaulting in your secrets manager. We'll include rotation best practices.
08:56 Rosa: Also want to confirm SAML attributes we need for RBAC mapping.
09:00 Priya: We'll include attribute mappings in the SSO guide.

09:20 Alex: Alright let's recap next steps — action items and owners: Alex to send SSO/SOC2 and pricing by Oct 4; Priya to schedule technical deep-dive and perf plan by Oct 8; Samir to share onboarding checklist and security contact; Mariner to confirm pilot dataset and SME by Oct 6.
09:45 Marcus: Sounds good.
09:50 Emily: Thanks all.
09:55 Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and links. Expect an email with attachments and scheduling invites.
10:05 End meeting.

Notes / Links mentioned: SSO/SAML guide (link in follow-up), SOC2 summary (will attach), onboarding checklist & onboarding timeline (will attach), perf test spreadsheet (to be shared by Priya).

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (product names like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes show up as "Redwood dedicate"), speaker overlap at 00:25-00:34, timestamps approximate.
